standard_prerequisites.name: Set
standard_prerequisites.statement: X is a set when every path type of X is a mere proposition, equivalently when it satisfies uniqueness of identity proofs.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the left hand side of the equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: Streicher Axiom K
standard_prerequisites.statement: X satisfies Axiom K when for every x and every loop p at x we have p equal to the reflexivity path.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the right hand side of the equivalence.

standard_prerequisites.name: Path induction
standard_prerequisites.statement: To prove a family of statements about an arbitrary path it suffices to prove the case of the reflexivity path.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the only tool used in the converse direction.

core_obligations: Show that Axiom K is a special case of uniqueness of identity proofs (source line 254).
For the converse fix x, y and two paths p and q and reduce the goal p = q by induction on q (source lines 255-256).
Recognise the reduced goal as exactly the Axiom K statement for the remaining loop (source lines 256-257).

proof_roadmap.step: Axiom K is an instance of uniqueness of identity proofs.
Converse by induction on one of the two paths, which leaves Axiom K.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled theorem at source lines 247-251 (book Theorem 7.2.1): a type is a set if and only if it satisfies Streicher Axiom K, that is, every loop at every point is equal to the reflexivity path. The proof (source lines 253-257) is short but the two directions are of different kinds: the forward direction is an immediate specialisation, while the converse has to reduce a statement about two arbitrary parallel paths to a statement about a single loop, which is done by induction on one of them; the statement itself gives no hint that this reduction is the whole content, nor that it is exactly where the loop of Axiom K appears.
